rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters define khushūʿ through inward acts such as fear and awe.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من جعله من أفعال القلوب كالخوف والرهبة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others define it through bodily stillness and not turning away.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعله من أفعال الجوارح كالسكون وترك الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers joining both: inward surrender and humility, attention to divine majesty, and a still, lowered gaze without turning right or left.
rows.anchor: منهم من جمع بين الأمرين وهو الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only bodily khushūʿ can be seen in a person; the heart's state remains invisible.
rows.anchor: ولكن الخشوع الذي يرى على الإنسان ليس إلا ما يتعلق بالجوارح فإن ما يتعلق بالقلب لا يرى

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
rows.claim: They report that Muslims and the Prophet once raised their eyes heavenward in prayer, then after this verse he lowered his gaze and kept it within his prayer place.
rows.anchor: قال : الحسن وابن سيرين كان المسلمون يرفعون أبصارهم إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says khushūʿ is obligatory in prayer, while his later discussion distinguishes spiritual acceptance from legal discharge.
rows.anchor: قلنا إنه عندنا واجب ويدل عليه أمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on the Qurʾān requires grasping its meaning; tarṭīl likewise means pausing over its wonders and meanings.
rows.anchor: والتدبر لا يتصور بدون الوقوف على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to remember Him is obligatory, and heedlessness contradicts remembrance, so a wholly heedless person cannot be establishing prayer for remembrance.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الأمر للوجوب والغفلة تضاد الذكر فمن غفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against being among the heedless is outwardly prohibitive and therefore supports requiring attentiveness.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن من الغافلين } ( الأعراف : 205 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requirement that intoxicated people know what they say also applies by analogy to a heedless person absorbed in worldly concerns.
rows.anchor: تعليل لنهي السكران وهو مطرد في الغافل المستغرق المهتم بالدنيا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying restricts khushūʿ to one who makes himself humble and lowly.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( إنما الخشوع لمن تمسكن وتواضع )

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A prayer that fails to restrain its performer from indecency only increases that person in distance from God; a heedless prayer does not restrain.
rows.anchor: من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says that some people who stand in prayer receive only fatigue and exertion, meaning the heedless.
rows.anchor: كم من قائم حظه من قيامه التعب والنصب

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A person receives from prayer only the portion he comprehends.
rows.anchor: ليس للعبد من صلاته إلا ما عقل

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī argues that a worshipper converses privately with God, while speech produced in heedlessness is not intimate address.
rows.anchor: قال الغزالي رحمه الله : المصلي يناجي ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrimage is arduous and disciplines people through hardship whether or not the heart is present, unlike prayer's intended intimate address.
rows.anchor: وكذا الحج أفعال شاقة ، وفيه من المجاهدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's remembrance is meant as intimate address to God; mere sounds have no sound purpose, and the tongue must express the heart's supplication.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن المقصود منه المناجاة وذلك لا يتحقق إلا إذا كان اللسان معبرا عما في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying guide us to the straight path with a heedless heart illustrates why prayer's recitation must be understood.
rows.anchor: وكان القلب غافلا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath to thank, praise, and petition someone is not fulfilled by reciting those phrases without intending to address that person; the analogy illustrates heedless prayer.
rows.anchor: ثم جرت الألفاظ الدالة على هذه المعاني على لسانه في اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bowing and prostration aim at magnifying God; without awareness they would be indistinguishable from prostrating to an idol, leaving only bodily movement.
rows.anchor: وأما الركوع والسجود فالمقصود منهما التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's central place among difficult acts of worship and its role distinguishing faith from unbelief show that its intended intimate address must accompany its outward actions.
rows.anchor: ويجب القتل بسببه على الخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists differ on whether the worshipper at the final salutation intends those present, absent people, or both; if its meaning merits reflection, the opening and glorifications merit it more.
rows.anchor: هل ينوي الحضور أو الغيبة والحضور معا

rows.speaker: المخالفون
rows.claim: Opponents object that requiring humility and khushūʿ conflicts with juristic consensus.
rows.anchor: واحتج المخالف بأن اشتراط الخضوع والخشوع على خلاف اجتماع الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that presence is required for acceptance and reward, not for legal discharge that removes the duty to repeat the prayer.
rows.anchor: أن الحضور عندنا ليس شرطا للأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning a borrowed garment properly discharges the obligation but earns praise, while throwing it back contemptuously still discharges it but earns blame; prayer can likewise be formally discharged yet blameworthy.
rows.anchor: فقد خرج عن العهدة واستحق المدح

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians agree that inward presence is necessary because intention to obey distinguishes prostration to God from an otherwise similar prostration to an idol.
rows.anchor: أما المتكلمون فقد اتفقوا على أنه لا بد من الحضور

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abū al-Layth says complete recitation avoids grammatical error and is performed reflectively.
rows.anchor: ذكر الفقيه أبو الليث رحمه الله في تنبيه الغافلين

rows.speaker: بشر الحافي
rows.claim: Bishr al-Ḥāfī says that whoever lacks khushūʿ has a corrupted prayer, as transmitted by al-Ghazālī from Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī.
rows.anchor: عن بشر الحافي أنه قال : من لم يخشع فسدت صلاته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that a prayer without the heart's presence is nearer to punishment.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن رحمه الله : كل صلاة لا يحضر فيها القلب

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿādh says that one who deliberately recognizes who is to his right and left while praying has no prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن معاذ بن جبل : من عرف من على يمينه وشماله متعمدا

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A transmitted Prophetic report says a person may receive only a sixth or tenth of a prayer, and receives only what he comprehends.
rows.anchor: إن العبد ليصلي الصلاة لا يكتب له سدسها ولا عشرها

rows.speaker: عبد الواحد بن زيد
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Zayd claims scholarly consensus that a person receives from prayer only what he comprehends.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الواحد بن زيد : أجمعت العلماء على أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if jurists broadly allow prayer without this presence, the stricter position of theologians and the scrupulous is safer.
rows.anchor: فهلا أخذت بالاحتياط فإن بعض العلماء اختار الإمامة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: One scholar chose to follow the imam to avoid being criticized by al-Shāfiʿī for omitting the Fātiḥa or by Abū Ḥanīfa for reciting it behind the imam.
rows.anchor: فقال : أخاف إن تركت الفاتحة أن يعاتبني الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transgressors are those who reach the furthest degree of transgression.
rows.anchor: يعني الكاملون في العدوان المتناهون فيه

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read the trust term in the singular.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير { * لأمانتهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entrusted object and the commitment one has undertaken are themselves called a trust and a covenant.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه يسمى الشيء المؤتمن عليه والمعاهد عليه أمانة وعهدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic commands to return trusts and not betray them illustrate the term's usage.
rows.anchor: لا تخونوا الله والرسول وتخونوا أماناتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rāʿī is one who tends, preserves, and improves what is entrusted to him.
rows.anchor: والراعي القائم على الشيء لحفظ وإصلاح كراعي الغنم وراعي الرعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust covers everything whose neglect counts as betrayal, including all worship, whether hidden itself or hidden in the manner of its performance.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الأمانة تتناول كل ما تركه يكون داخلا في الخيانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of worship entrusted to a person include fasting, ritual bathing after sexual impurity, and completing ablution properly.
rows.anchor: لأنها إما أن تخفي أصلا كالصوم وغسل الجنابة وإسباغ الوضوء

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying calls the person who does not complete his prayer the greatest betrayer.
rows.anchor: أعظم الناس خيانة من لم يتم صلاته

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says trust is the first thing lost from religion and prayer the last.
rows.anchor: أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الأمانة وآخر ما تفقدون الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deposits, contracts, and other commitments made by deed or speech must be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: ومن جملة ذلك ما يلتزمه بفعل أو قول فيلزمه الوفاء به كالودائع والعقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is also entrusted to honor the words by which slaves are emancipated and women are made unlawful to him.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك الأقوال التي يحرم بها العبيد والنساء لأنه مؤتمن في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Covenant includes contracts, oaths, and vows.
rows.anchor: وأما العهد فإنه دخل فيه العقود والإيمان والنذور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping these trusts and covenants counts toward attaining success.
rows.anchor: فبين سبحانه أن مراعاة هذه الأمور والقيام بها معتبر في حصول الفلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's repeated mention is deliberate: khushūʿ describes the worshipper during prayer, whereas preservation concerns care between prayers and the regular completion of their conditions.
rows.anchor: لأن الخشوع والمحافظة متغايران غير متلازمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preserving prayer means maintaining its time, purity, pillars, and completion as a consistent practice.
rows.anchor: بل المراد بالمحافظة التعهد لشروطها من وقت وطهارة وغيرهما والقيام على أركانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī offers three explanations for calling the reward and Garden inheritance.
rows.anchor: لم سمي ما يجدونه من الثواب والجنة بالميراث

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says God prepared for every accountable person a place in Hell if disobedient and in the Garden if obedient; when some disbelieve, their forfeited place passes to believers like inheritance.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو أبين على ما يقال فيه وهو : أنه لا مكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that God may transfer to a believer the station that would have belonged to that same person had he obeyed, with the stations adjusted accordingly.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع أنه تعالى جعل ما هو منزلة لهذا المؤمن بعينه منزلة لذلك الكافر لو أطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the Garden without accounting or measuring its portions resembles an heir's acquisition of property.
rows.anchor: أن انتقال الجنة إليهم بدون محاسبة ومعرفة بمقاديره يشبه انتقال المال إلى الوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden was Adam's dwelling, so its passing to his descendants resembles inheritance.
rows.anchor: أن الجنة كانت مسكن أبينا آدم عليه السلام فإذا انتقلت إلى أولاده صار ذلك شبيها بالميراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven listed qualities need not enumerate fasting, pilgrimage, and purity because trust and covenant encompass all duties and prohibitions, while purity falls under preserving prayer.
rows.anchor: يأتي على جميع الواجبات من الأفعال والتروك كما قدمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although inheritors sounds exclusive, that implication is set aside because children, the insane, youths, houris, and sinful believers after pardon also enter the Garden.
rows.anchor: يفيد الحصر لكنه يجب ترك العمل به لأنه ثبت أن الجنة يدخلها الأطفال والمجانين والولدان والحور العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws means Garden in Ethiopic, or according to another view in the language of the Romans.
rows.anchor: الفردوس هو الجنة بلسان الحبشة وقيل بلسان الروم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī transmits from the Prophet that Firdaws is the enclosure of the Merciful containing rivers and trees.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( الفردوس مقصورة الرحمن فيها الأنهار والأشجار )

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abū Umāma transmits the Prophet's instruction to ask God for Firdaws, the highest Garden, whose inhabitants hear the Throne's creaking.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عنه عليه السلام أنه قال : ( سلوا الله الفردوس فإنها أعلى الجنان

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī says these qualities define believers because, on his view, faith is a legal name for performing every obligation.
rows.anchor: ادعى القاضي أن الأمر كذلك بناء على مذهبه أن الإيمان اسم شرعي موضوع لأداء كل الواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the verse does not establish that these qualities are included in the word believers, just as calling people intelligent and just does not put those traits inside the word people.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا لا يدل على أن الزكاة والعدالة داخلان في مسمى الناس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says the Garden of Eden spoke the opening words after God created it and commanded it to speak.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( لما خلق الله تعالى جنة عدن

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that God made Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted the tree Ṭūbā with His hand, then commanded it to speak and it uttered the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب : ( خلق الله آدم بيده وكتب التوراة بيده وغرس شجرة طوبى بيده

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says prayer praises and intercedes for the one who performs it well, but calls down loss on the one who neglects it.
rows.anchor: إذا أحسن العبد الوضوء وصلى الصلاة لوقتها وحافظ على ركوعها وسجودها ومواقيتها قالت حفظك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden's speech means that it has been prepared for believers, as in the Qurʾānic personification of heaven and earth saying they came willingly.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به أنها أعدت للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's creating the Garden with His hand means He personally undertook its creation rather than delegating it.
rows.anchor: وأما أنه تعالى خلق الجنة بيده فالمراد تولى خلقها لا أنه وكله إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's praise is figurative: prayer consists of movements and stillnesses that cannot literally take form and speak, like saying a benefactor's kindness speaks gratitude.
rows.anchor: الصلاة حركات وسكنات ولا يصح عليها أن تتصور

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that the Garden is uncreated because its produce is described as everlasting; he therefore reads the inheritance verse as referring to a Garden created at the Resurrection or to a later saying.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي دل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects al-Qāḍī's interpretation because there is no better reason to insert a future creation into the inheritance verse than into the verse about everlasting produce.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف لأنه ليس إضمار ما ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī takes everlasting produce as referring to the Resurrection and holds the Garden is already created, citing that it has been prepared for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: فنحن نتمسك في أن الجنة مخلوقة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the warning was spoken only after the people rejected the prophet's proof, to frighten them with the threatened punishment.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { أفلا تتقون } غير موصول بالأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the warning can instead continue the opening speech: seeing them turn from God toward idols, the prophet called them to worship God and warned of punishment.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون موصولا بالكلام الأول بأن رآهم معرضين عن عبادة الله مشتغلين بعبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī identifies three traits of the people: disbelief in the Creator, denial of the Hereafter, and immersion in worldly luxury; he glosses their being made affluent as being favored.
rows.anchor: هي شر الصفات : أولها : الكفر بالخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this context, making them affluent means granting them worldly ease and favor.
rows.anchor: وقال الملا من قومه } أي نعمناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounts without a conjunction answer an implied question about what the people said; the conjunction here coordinates their false speech with the prophet's true speech.
rows.anchor: الذي بغير واو على تقدير سؤال سائل قال فما قال قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction in this account conveys that the true and false speeches occurred together in the same episode.
rows.anchor: وأما الذي مع الواو فعطف لما قالوه على ما قاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their first objection is that the messenger is a human who eats and drinks as they do; they treat obedience to him as a loss because it brings no return benefit.
rows.anchor: أي من مشروبكم أو حذف منه لدلالة ما قبله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call following a human messenger a loss despite not considering idol worship a loss.
rows.anchor: ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم إنكم إذا لخاسرون

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their resurrection objection asks whether they will be returned alive after death and decomposition in order to be recompensed.
rows.anchor: أنكم مخرجون } معادون أحياء للمجازاة

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking whether resurrection will occur, they intensify their denial with the expression meaning how far-fetched.
rows.anchor: { هيهات هيهات لما توعدون } ثم أكدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By saying we die and live, they mean that some people die while others live, denying any individual return or resurrection.
rows.anchor: بل أرادوا أن البعض يموت والبعض يحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They conclude that there is no resurrection and then infer that the prophet fabricated a lie against God and that they will not believe him.
rows.anchor: ولما فرغوا من الطعن في صحة الحشر بنوا عليه الطعن في نبوته

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not answer these objections in this passage because their errors are evident; omnipotence and knowledge entail His ability to resurrect.
rows.anchor: ولا يستبعد الحشر لوجهين : الأول

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without resurrection, the strong could oppress the weak without redress, which is unfitting for the Wise God; the Qurʾān says each soul will be recompensed for its striving.
rows.anchor: تسليط القوى على الضعيف في الدنيا ظلما

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated anna in the promise clause emphasizes the assertion; the intervening time phrase makes the repetition apt, and makhrujūn predicates the first clause.
rows.anchor: ثنى إنكم للتوكيد وحسن ذلك الفصل

words: أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading omits the intervening phrase about dying and being dust and bones.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : { وكنتم ترابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression hayhāt is read with fatḥa or kasra, with or without tanwīn, and with sukūn in pause.
rows.anchor: قرىء { هيهات } بالفتح والكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in in hiya has no clear antecedent until the following words explain it; the underlying wording is in al-ḥayātu illā ḥayātunā al-dunyā.
rows.anchor: ضمير لا يعلم ما يعني به إلا بما يتلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun replaces al-ḥayāh because the predicate makes its referent clear.
rows.anchor: ثم وضع هي موضع الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that no life exists except the present worldly life.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative in is used with hiya in a genus-denying sense, equivalent to lā negating the genus.
rows.anchor: إن النافية دخلت على هي التي في معنى الحياة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poet's line, “the soul: whatever burden you give it, it bears,” illustrates use of a pronoun whose sense is supplied by the predicate.
rows.anchor: هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the messenger despaired of acceptance by both leaders and ordinary people, he appealed to God for help against their denial.
rows.anchor: ذلك الرسول لما يئس من قبول الأكابر والأصاغر فزع إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened regret likely begins when signs of destruction appear; their remorse then comes too late, as desperate faith will not benefit them.
rows.anchor: الأقرب أن يكون المراد بأن يظهر لهم علامات الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī lists four views of the cry: Gabriel's deadly shout, an earthquake reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, death or punishment according to al-Ḥasan, and overwhelming punishment; he prefers the literal first view.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام صاح بهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the cry with the earthquake.
rows.anchor: الصيحة هي الرجفة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the cry is the punishment itself or death, as when one says that a person was called and answered.
rows.anchor: الصيحة هي نفس العذاب والموت كما يقال فيمن يموت : دعي فأجاب عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line about time crying out at the Barmak family illustrates the cry as an overwhelming punishment.
rows.anchor: صاخ الزمان بآل برمك صيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq means God destroyed them justly, as the phrase judging by truth describes a just judge.
rows.anchor: فمعناه أنه دمرهم بالعدل

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says bi-l-ḥaqq means something irresistible, as in the verse about death's stupor arriving with truth.
rows.anchor: وقال المفضل : بالحق أي بما لا يدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ is the flood-carried debris of decayed, blackened leaves and twigs.
rows.anchor: فالغثاء حميل السيل مما بلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same word describes what God made of the vegetation in another verse.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { فجعله غثاء أحوى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal nouns buʿdan, suḥqan, and damran stand in place of verbs and are accusative under verbs whose explicit forms are not used, as Sibawayh explains.
rows.anchor: وهي من جملة المصادر التي قال سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan means that they perished; the word can be pronounced with either fatḥa or sukūn on the ʿayn, like rushdan.
rows.anchor: يقال بعد بعدا وبعدا بفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿdan is like a curse that distances them from goodness; God says it to scorn and humiliate them, and their worldly punishment signals an even greater exclusion from bliss in the Hereafter, warning later generations.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة اللعن الذي هو التبعيد من الخير
